seen.extent: three lines of 30 digits (90 digits), written in ink without spacing on plain letter paper, per the printed request
seen.cipher: Read the OCR text of the column: 'The figures below, which appear to be some kind of code or cipher, were found by a friend of mine while examining some valuable old letters and papers', signed T. F. Riddell, Champaign, Ill.; the three digit lines are printed (OCR has two digit errors, so the digits must be taken from Schmeh's transcription); the expert Francis H. Bent offers no solution and only refers the writer to the War Department, Bureau of Investigation and a crime lab. No decipherment is printed with it.

1304.closed: Every number line on the back of the cover has its plaintext letters written beneath it in the writer's own hand (caisson, canteen, potteswood struck out, louse, pirated, and 'itch', 'trout', 'Trevy' as the odd ones), which is an interlinear decipherment on the leaf; the cipher is a self-glossed homophonic jotting, so nothing remains to solve beyond the table the glosses already give.
